result.topic_en: The page has no writing of its own; it shows faint mirror-image bleed-through of algebraic calculations from the other side of the leaf, apparently relating y, e, p, q through square roots and a polar substitution 1+p = a cos A, q = a sin A.
result.transcription:
[Page appears blank apart from faint mirror-reversed show-through from the reverse side; tentative reading of the reversed text:]

Auflösung der Gleichung[?] ...
$\cos f - \ldots = p + \ldots q$ [?]
...
$(1-ee)(yy-1) = qq$
$yy + ee - 1 - eeyy = qq$
$yy + ee = 1 + pp + qq$ [?]
$y + e = \sqrt{(1+p)^2 + qq}$
$y - e = \sqrt{(1-p)^2 + qq}$

$ss + \sigma\sigma = yy - ee = \sqrt{((1+p)^2+qq)((1-p)^2+qq)}$ [?]
$ss - \sigma\sigma = \ldots = \sqrt{(1-pp-qq)}$ [?]
$1+p = a \cos A \quad 1-p = b \cos B$ [?]
$q = a \sin A \quad q = b \sin B$ [?]

$ss + \sigma\sigma = ab$ [?]
$ss - \sigma\sigma = ab \cos(A+B)$ [?]

$s = \sqrt{ab}\,\cos\tfrac12(A+B)$ [?]
$\sigma = \sqrt{ab}\,\sin\tfrac12(A+B)$ [?]

$y = \tfrac12(a+b)$
$e = \tfrac12(a-b)$

methods.what: Expressing y+e and y-e as square roots of sums of squares
Solution for y and e as half-sum and half-difference of a and b
